metadata.title: Layer Normalization
metadata.authors: Jimmy Lei Ba, Jamie Ryan Kiros, Geoffrey E. Hinton

nodes.name: Feed-forward neural network summed inputs
nodes.statement: For the $l^{th}$ hidden layer with weight matrix $W^l$ and bottom-up inputs $h^l$: $a^l_i = {w^l_i}^\T h^l$ and $h^{l+1}_i = f(a^l_i + b^l_i)$, where $f(\cdot)$ is element-wise non-linearity and $b^l_i$ is a scalar bias.
nodes.statement_clean: Definition of the summed input to neuron i in layer l of a feed-forward network and its activation.

nodes.name: Batch normalization statistics
nodes.statement: $\bar{a}^l_i = \frac{g^l_i}{\sigma^l_i}(a^l_i - \mu^l_i)$ with $\mu^l_i = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim P(x)}[a^l_i]$ and $\sigma^l_i = \sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{x \sim P(x)}[(a^l_i - \mu^l_i)^2]}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Batch normalization rescales summed inputs using mean and standard deviation taken across the data distribution, with a per-neuron gain.

nodes.name: Layer normalization statistics
nodes.statement: $\mu^l = \frac{1}{H}\sum_{i=1}^H a^l_i$ and $\sigma^l = \sqrt{\frac{1}{H}\sum_{i=1}^H (a^l_i - \mu^l)^2}$, where $H$ is the number of hidden units in the layer.
nodes.statement_clean: Layer normalization computes mean and standard deviation over all hidden units in the same layer for a single training case.

nodes.name: Layer normalization function $LN$
nodes.statement: $LN(z;\alpha,\beta) = \frac{(z-\mu)}{\sigma}\odot\alpha + \beta$ with $\mu = \frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D z_i$ and $\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D (z_i-\mu)^2}$, mapping $\mathbb{R}^D \to \mathbb{R}^D$ with adaptive gains $\alpha$ and biases $\beta$.
nodes.statement_clean: The layer normalization operator as a parameterized function with adaptive per-dimension gains and biases.

nodes.name: Layer-normalized RNN recurrent layer
nodes.statement: $h^t = f\big[\frac{g}{\sigma^t}\odot(a^t - \mu^t) + b\big]$ with $a^t = W_{hh}h^{t-1} + W_{xh}x^t$, $\mu^t = \frac{1}{H}\sum_i a_i^t$, $\sigma^t = \sqrt{\frac{1}{H}\sum_i(a_i^t-\mu^t)^2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Layer normalization applied to the recurrent layer of a standard RNN at each time-step, with one shared gain and bias.

nodes.name: Generalized Linear Model (GLM) log-likelihood
nodes.statement: $\log P(y|x;w,b) = \frac{(a+b)y - \eta(a+b)}{\phi} + c(y,\phi)$ with $\mathbb{E}[y|x] = f(a+b) = f(w^\T x + b)$ and $\mathrm{Var}[y|x] = \phi f'(a+b)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Exponential-family GLM parameterized by weight vector $w$ and scalar bias $b$, with transfer function $f$.

nodes.name: Fisher information matrix (KL Riemannian metric)
nodes.statement: $ds^2 = D_{KL}[P(y|x;\theta)\,\|\,P(y|x;\theta+\delta)] \approx \frac{1}{2}\delta^\T F(\theta)\delta$ with $F(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{x,y}\big[\frac{\partial \log P}{\partial \theta}\frac{\partial \log P}{\partial \theta}^\T\big]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Second-order Taylor approximation of the KL divergence yields the Fisher information matrix as the Riemannian metric on the parameter manifold.

nodes.name: GLM Fisher information matrix
nodes.statement: For multi-dimensional GLM with $\theta = \mathrm{vec}([W,b]^\T)$: $F(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim P(x)}\big[\frac{\mathrm{Cov}[y|x]}{\phi^2}\otimes\begin{bmatrix}xx^\T & x \\ x^\T & 1\end{bmatrix}\big]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fisher information matrix for a multi-dimensional GLM is the expected Kronecker product of the output covariance and the data feature outer product.

nodes.name: Normalized-GLM Fisher information matrix $\bar{F}$
nodes.statement: $\bar{F}_{ij} = \mathbb{E}_x\big[\frac{\mathrm{Cov}[y_i,y_j|x]}{\phi^2}\,M_{ij}(g,\sigma,\chi,a,\mu)\big]$, where $\chi_i = x - \frac{\partial \mu_i}{\partial w_i} - \frac{a_i-\mu_i}{\sigma_i}\frac{\partial \sigma_i}{\partial w_i}$ and $M_{ij}$ is the $3\times 3$ block in Eq. (nfisher).
nodes.statement_clean: Block of the Fisher information matrix for a normalized GLM with parameters $(W,b,g)$, with corrections from the dependence of $\mu_i,\sigma_i$ on $w_i$.

nodes.name: Common normalization form
nodes.section: 5.1 Invariance under weights and data transformations
nodes.statement: $h_i = f\big(\frac{g_i}{\sigma_i}(a_i - \mu_i) + b_i\big)$, the common form for batch, weight, and layer normalization (with $\mu,\sigma$ defined per scheme; weight-norm uses $\mu=0$, $\sigma=\|w\|_2$).

nodes.name: Layer normalization is invariant to weight matrix re-scaling and re-centering
nodes.statement: If $W' = \delta W + \mathbf{1}\gamma^\T$, then under layer normalization $h' = f(\frac{g}{\sigma'}(W'x - \mu') + b) = f(\frac{g}{\sigma}(Wx - \mu) + b) = h$.
nodes.statement_clean: Scaling the entire weight matrix and adding a constant to every incoming-weight row leaves layer-normalized outputs unchanged.
assumptions: Layer normalization (Eq. 3) is applied to summed inputs
conclusions: $h'(x) = h(x)$, i.e. the model output is invariant to the $(\delta,\gamma)$ transformation of $W$

nodes.name: Layer normalization is invariant to per-example input re-scaling
nodes.statement: If $x' = \delta x$, then $h'_i = f(\frac{g_i}{\sigma'}(w_i^\T x' - \mu') + b_i) = f(\frac{g_i}{\delta\sigma}(\delta w_i^\T x - \delta\mu) + b_i) = h_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Re-scaling a single training case by $\delta$ leaves the layer-normalized prediction unchanged.
assumptions: Layer normalization is applied to the summed inputs of a single training case
conclusions: $h'(x') = h(x)$, i.e. the prediction is invariant to per-example input scaling

nodes.name: Invariance summary table for batch / weight / layer normalization
nodes.statement: Across six transformations (weight matrix re-scaling, weight matrix re-centering, weight vector re-scaling, dataset re-scaling, dataset re-centering, single training case re-scaling), batch norm is invariant to weight-matrix re-scaling, weight-vector re-scaling, dataset re-scaling and re-centering; weight norm is invariant to weight-matrix and weight-vector re-scaling; layer norm is invariant to weight-matrix re-scaling and re-centering, dataset re-scaling, and single training case re-scaling.
nodes.statement_clean: Table 1: each normalization scheme has a distinct set of invariances.
assumptions: Three normalization schemes share the form $h_i = f(\frac{g_i}{\sigma_i}(a_i-\mu_i)+b_i)$ with scheme-specific $(\mu_i,\sigma_i)$
conclusions: Layer normalization is the only one of the three invariant to single training case re-scaling
Layer normalization is the only one of the three invariant to weight-matrix re-centering
Batch normalization is the only one invariant to dataset re-centering

nodes.name: Implicit learning-rate reduction via weight-norm growth
nodes.statement: If $\|w_i\|$ doubles, the model output is unchanged but the curvature of $\bar{F}$ along the $w_i$ direction shrinks by a factor of $\tfrac{1}{2}$ because $\sigma_i$ also doubles, so the same gradient step produces a smaller change in orientation of large-norm weights.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalization induces an implicit early-stopping effect: the effective learning rate for a weight vector is inversely proportional to its norm.
assumptions: Normalized GLM with Fisher information matrix $\bar{F}$ as in Eq. (nfisher)
conclusions: The Fisher block along $w_i$ scales as $1/\|w_i\|$, reducing the effective learning rate as the weight norm grows

nodes.name: Gain-direction Riemannian metric depends only on prediction error
nodes.section: 5.2.2 Learning the magnitude of incoming weights
nodes.statement: For batch and layer normalized GLMs, $ds^2 = \frac{1}{2}\delta_g^\T \,\mathbb{E}_x[\mathrm{Cov}[y|x]/\phi^2]\, \delta_g$ (batch) or a related expression depending on $(a_i-\mu)/\sigma$ (layer), so updates along the gain parameters depend only on the magnitude of the prediction error, not on the input scale.
nodes.statement_clean: Learning the magnitude of incoming weights through gain parameters in normalized models is robust to the scaling of inputs and parameters.
assumptions: Gradient update changes only the gain parameter by $\delta_g$
conclusions: The KL change $ds^2$ along the gain direction is proportional to expected output covariance, independent of input norm
Standard (un-normalized) GLM has $ds^2$ depending on $a_i a_j / (\|w_i\|\|w_j\|)$, which is input-dependent

nodes.name: Layer Normalization (LN) operator
nodes.statement: Given activation vector $z \in \mathbb{R}^D$ and adaptive gain/bias $(\alpha,\beta)$, compute mean and variance across the $D$ coordinates of $z$, normalize, then re-scale and shift coordinate-wise.
input: Activation vector $z \in \mathbb{R}^D$ for a single training case at one layer / time-step

nodes.name: Layer-normalized LSTM
nodes.section: Supplementary Material (Teaching machines to read and comprehend; handwriting)
nodes.statement: An LSTM in which the pre-activations from $W_h h_{t-1}$ and $W_x x_t$ and the cell state $c_t$ are individually layer-normalized using $LN$ with separate gain/bias parameters.
input: Input $x_t$ and previous hidden state $h_{t-1}$, previous cell state $c_{t-1}$
Weights $W_h, W_x$, bias $b$, three pairs of LN parameters $(\alpha_1,\beta_1),(\alpha_2,\beta_2),(\alpha_3,\beta_3)$
output: Updated cell state $c_t$ and hidden state $h_t$
nodes.pseudocode:
$(f_t,i_t,o_t,g_t)^\T = LN(W_h h_{t-1};\alpha_1,\beta_1) + LN(W_x x_t;\alpha_2,\beta_2) + b$
$c_t = \sigma(f_t)\odot c_{t-1} + \sigma(i_t)\odot \tanh(g_t)$
$h_t = \sigma(o_t)\odot \tanh(LN(c_t;\alpha_3,\beta_3))$

nodes.name: Layer-normalized GRU
nodes.statement: A GRU variant in which $W_h h_{t-1}$, $W_x x_t$, $W x_t$, and $U h_{t-1}$ are each separately layer-normalized using $LN$ with distinct gain/bias parameters.
input: Weights $W_h, W_x, W, U$, four pairs of LN parameters $(\alpha_i,\beta_i)_{i=1}^4$
nodes.pseudocode:
$(z_t, r_t)^\T = LN(W_h h_{t-1};\alpha_1,\beta_1) + LN(W_x x_t;\alpha_2,\beta_2)$
$\hat{h}_t = \tanh(LN(W x_t;\alpha_3,\beta_3) + \sigma(r_t)\odot LN(U h_{t-1};\alpha_4,\beta_4))$
$h_t = (1-\sigma(z_t)) h_{t-1} + \sigma(z_t) \hat{h}_t$

nodes.name: Layer-normalized DRAW LSTM
nodes.section: Supplementary Material (Modeling binarized MNIST using DRAW)
nodes.statement: An LSTM used in DRAW where layer normalization is applied only to the cell state $c_t$ (not to the pre-activation gates).
input: Input $x_t$ and previous hidden state $h_{t-1}$, previous cell state $c_{t-1}$
Weights $W_h, W_x$, bias $b$, single pair of LN parameters $(\alpha,\beta)$
output: Updated cell state $c_t$ and hidden state $h_t$
nodes.pseudocode:
$(f_t,i_t,o_t,g_t)^\T = W_h h_{t-1} + W_x x_t + b$
$c_t = \sigma(f_t)\odot c_{t-1} + \sigma(i_t)\odot \tanh(g_t)$
$h_t = \sigma(o_t)\odot \tanh(LN(c_t;\alpha,\beta))$

nodes.name: Reducing covariate shift / training time in deep neural networks
nodes.statement: Design a per-layer normalization scheme that reduces internal covariate shift, accelerates training of deep networks (including RNNs), and works in the small-batch and online regimes where batch normalization is impractical.

nodes.name: Order-embeddings of images and language (MSCOCO)
nodes.section: 6.1 Order embeddings of images and language
nodes.statement: Layer normalization applied to the GRU encoder of the order-embeddings model on Microsoft COCO improves Caption Retrieval R@1 from 46.6 to 48.5 and Image Retrieval R@1 from 37.8 to 38.9, and reaches the best validation score in 60% of the baseline's training time.

nodes.name: Attentive reader on CNN corpus (question answering)
nodes.section: 6.2 Teaching machines to read and comprehend
nodes.statement: On a unidirectional attentive-reader QA model trained on the CNN corpus, layer normalization both trains faster and converges to a better validation result than the baseline and recurrent batch normalization variants, and is robust to gain initialization (1.0 outperforms 0.1, unlike recurrent BN).

nodes.name: Skip-thought vectors on BookCorpus
nodes.statement: Training a 2400-dimensional skip-thoughts encoder on BookCorpus with layer normalization yields a speedup over baseline and improves downstream tasks (SICK, MR, CR, SUBJ, MPQA) after 1M iterations, with further gains after a month of training.

nodes.name: DRAW on binarized MNIST
nodes.statement: On a DRAW model with 64 glimpses and 256 LSTM hidden units trained on the fixed-binarization MNIST, layer normalization yields nearly $2\times$ faster convergence; baseline reaches $82.36$ nats and LN reaches $82.09$ nats test variational log-likelihood after 200 epochs.

nodes.name: Handwriting sequence generation (IAM-OnDB)
nodes.statement: On the IAM Online Handwriting Database with sequences of average length $\sim 700$ and mini-batch size 8, a 3-layer 400-cell LSTM with layer normalization converges to comparable log-likelihood as the baseline but much faster.

nodes.name: Permutation-invariant MNIST classification
nodes.statement: On a 784-1000-1000-10 feed-forward network for permutation-invariant MNIST trained with Adam, layer normalization is robust across batch-sizes 128 and 4 and converges faster than batch normalization applied to all layers.

nodes.name: Convolutional networks (preliminary)
nodes.statement: Preliminary ConvNet experiments show that layer normalization speeds up training over an unnormalized baseline but is outperformed by batch normalization, because boundary-receptive-field hidden units have very different statistics from interior units.

nodes.name: Layer normalization is not a re-parameterization
nodes.statement: Unlike weight normalization or batch normalization with expected statistics, the layer-normalized model is not a re-parameterization of the original feed-forward network, and therefore has different invariance properties.

nodes.name: Stable hidden-to-hidden dynamics in RNNs
nodes.statement: Because layer normalization makes the recurrent layer invariant to re-scaling of all summed inputs, it prevents the average magnitude of summed inputs from drifting at each time-step, mitigating exploding/vanishing gradients.

nodes.name: Same computation at training and test time
nodes.statement: Unlike batch normalization, layer normalization performs exactly the same computation at training and test time and imposes no constraint on mini-batch size; it can be used in pure online learning with batch size 1.

nodes.name: Substitute the transformed weights into the layer-normalized output
nodes.statement: Replace $W$ by $W' = \delta W + \mathbf{1}\gamma^\T$ in $h' = f(\frac{g}{\sigma'}(W' x - \mu') + b)$ to expand the pre-activation as $(\delta W + \mathbf{1}\gamma^\T) x = \delta W x + (\gamma^\T x)\mathbf{1}$.

nodes.name: New mean and standard deviation under the transformation
nodes.statement: Show that $\mu' = \delta\mu + \gamma^\T x$ and $\sigma' = \delta\sigma$, since adding $(\gamma^\T x)\mathbf{1}$ shifts every coordinate by the same constant and scaling by $\delta$ scales both mean and standard deviation by $\delta$.

nodes.name: Cancel $\delta$ and the constant shift
nodes.statement: Substitute $\mu' = \delta\mu + \gamma^\T x$, $\sigma' = \delta\sigma$, and $W' x = \delta W x + (\gamma^\T x)\mathbf{1}$ into the LN expression; the constant shift cancels and $\delta$ cancels in the ratio, yielding $f(\frac{g}{\sigma}(Wx - \mu) + b) = h$.

nodes.name: Express normalization statistics under input scaling
nodes.statement: With $x' = \delta x$, the summed input becomes $w_i^\T x' = \delta w_i^\T x$, so $\mu' = \delta \mu$ and $\sigma' = \delta \sigma$.

nodes.name: Cancel $\delta$ in the LN ratio
nodes.statement: Substitute into $h'_i = f(\frac{g_i}{\sigma'}(w_i^\T x' - \mu') + b_i) = f(\frac{g_i}{\delta\sigma}(\delta w_i^\T x - \delta\mu) + b_i) = f(\frac{g_i}{\sigma}(w_i^\T x - \mu) + b_i) = h_i$.

nodes.name: Compute layer mean
nodes.statement: $\mu \gets \frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D z_i$

nodes.name: Compute layer standard deviation
nodes.statement: $\sigma \gets \sqrt{\frac{1}{D}\sum_{i=1}^D (z_i - \mu)^2}$

nodes.name: Affine re-scale and shift
nodes.statement: Return $\frac{(z-\mu)}{\sigma}\odot \alpha + \beta$.

nodes.name: Compute and layer-normalize gate pre-activations
nodes.statement: $(f_t,i_t,o_t,g_t)^\T = LN(W_h h_{t-1};\alpha_1,\beta_1) + LN(W_x x_t;\alpha_2,\beta_2) + b$

nodes.name: Update cell state
nodes.statement: $c_t = \sigma(f_t)\odot c_{t-1} + \sigma(i_t)\odot \tanh(g_t)$

nodes.name: Layer-normalize cell state and emit hidden state
nodes.statement: $h_t = \sigma(o_t)\odot \tanh(LN(c_t;\alpha_3,\beta_3))$

nodes.name: Compute layer-normalized gate pre-activations
nodes.statement: $(z_t, r_t)^\T = LN(W_h h_{t-1};\alpha_1,\beta_1) + LN(W_x x_t;\alpha_2,\beta_2)$

nodes.name: Compute candidate hidden state
nodes.statement: $\hat{h}_t = \tanh(LN(W x_t;\alpha_3,\beta_3) + \sigma(r_t)\odot LN(U h_{t-1};\alpha_4,\beta_4))$

nodes.name: Update hidden state via gated combination
nodes.statement: $h_t = (1-\sigma(z_t)) h_{t-1} + \sigma(z_t) \hat{h}_t$

nodes.name: Compute gate pre-activations (no LN)
nodes.statement: $(f_t,i_t,o_t,g_t)^\T = W_h h_{t-1} + W_x x_t + b$

nodes.name: Update cell state
nodes.statement: $c_t = \sigma(f_t)\odot c_{t-1} + \sigma(i_t)\odot \tanh(g_t)$

nodes.name: Apply LN to cell state and emit hidden state
nodes.statement: $h_t = \sigma(o_t)\odot \tanh(LN(c_t;\alpha,\beta))$
